chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Ibrahim ibn Maymoun, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I perform Hajj one year and my associate performs Hajj one year.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'What is preventing you from the Hajj, O Ibrahim?' I said, 'I am not free for that, may I be sacrificed for you. I tend to give in charity with five hundred in place of that.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The Hajj is superior.' I said, 'A thousand?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The Hajj is superior.' I said, 'So a thousand and five hundred?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The Hajj is superior.' I said, 'Two thousand?'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'Is there, in your two thousand, a circumambulation of the House?' I said, 'No.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Is there, in your two thousand, a Sa'ee between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa?' I said, 'No.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Is there, in your two thousand, a pausing at Arafat?' I said, 'No.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Is there, in your two thousand, pelting of the rocks?' I said, 'No.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Is there, in your two thousand, the rituals?' I said, 'No.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The Hajj is superior.'
ai.seo_question: Why is performing Hajj better than giving its cost in charity?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the superiority of the physical performance of Hajj over its monetary equivalent in charity, emphasizing that the ritual's spiritual merit is inextricably linked to the bodily acts of worship. By systematically questioning whether the sum includes Tawaf, Sa'ee, Wuquf, and Ramy, the Imam highlights that charity cannot substitute for the specific devotional movements that constitute the pillar of Islam. This dialogue underscores the Shia scholarly view that while charity is virtuous, the Hajj holds a unique ontological status as a physical manifestation of submission that money alone cannot replicate.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Ibrahim Bin Maymoun who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I perform Hajj one year and my associate performs Hajj one year’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What is preventing you from the Hajj, O Ibrahim?’ I said, ‘I am not free for that, may I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>. I tend to give in charity with five hundred in place of that’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Hajj is superior’. I said, ‘A thousand?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Hajj is superior’. I said, ‘So a thousand and five hundred?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Hajj is superior’. I said, ‘Two thousand?’

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Is there, in your two thousand, a circumambulation of the House (Kabah)?’ I said, ‘No’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Is there, in your two thousand, a Sa’ee between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa’. I said, ‘No’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Is there, in your two thousand, a pausing at Arafat?’ I said, ‘No’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Is there, in your two thousand, pelting of the rocks?’ I said, ‘No’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Is there, in your two thousand, the rituals?’ I said, ‘No’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Hajj is superior’.
en.sarwar: 28. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jundab who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ’
Al-Hajj is Jihad (hard work for the cause of Allah) of the weak people.’
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, then placed his hand on his chest and said, ‘We are the weak people, (we) are weak.’”
